cohort: Pregnant women with cardiac diseases (either pre-existing or newly diagnosed during pregnancy) at a tertiary care center in Karnataka, India.
finding: Cardiac disease complicating pregnancy had a significant impact, with 16.66% maternal mortality due to cardiac failure and cardiopulmonary arrest, along with adverse perinatal outcomes including preterm delivery, NICU admission, IUGR, and perinatal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Among the study participants, 41.66% had vaginal delivery, 16.66% had assisted instrumental vaginal delivery, and 16.66% were delivered by C-section.
